findings.why_it_matters: In an index the leading indent is the ONLY thing that marks a sub-entry as belonging to its parent. Flattening it detaches sub-items from their parents and promotes them to look like top-level index terms. The transcription is also self-inconsistent about this: pages 1237, 1238, 1239 and 1243 DO preserve the level with   runs, while pages 1235, 1236, 1240, 1241, 1242, 1244, 1245, 1246 (and the right-hand 'Category of data' block on 1237, md lines 64-79) drop it entirely. The worst reading arises on page 1244, where the sub-entry 'FILE-CONTROL paragraph 312' (under FILE STATUS clause) is flattened and lands immediately above the genuine top-level entry 'FILE-CONTROL paragraph 311', so the two read as a contradictory duplicate. Index only - no normative text is affected.
findings.suggested_repair: Apply the same  -per-level indentation scheme already used on pages 1237/1238/1239/1243 to the flattened index pages 1235, 1236, 1240, 1241, 1242, 1244, 1245, 1246, and to the 'Category of data' block on 1237. One level = 4  , matching the existing convention.
